title: Cory Johnson:
title_short: Cory Johnson · We Are Not Past Tense
headline: NIWRC's development officer names the thing people get wrong about Native people, in Oklahoma City, the heart of Indian Country: we are not past tense. We are still here.
story: Cory Johnson is NIWRC's Development and Strategic Impact Officer and he organised the reception. Asked what people get wrong, he answered without a pause: teepees, the 1840s, horses. Then he turned it: urban Natives, doctors, teachers, right here. This cut is that turn, with the DVAM line as the reason it matters in October.
This is a different cut from his Durham interview in July (NIWRCDurhamCoryJohnson001, Specialty Institute). Nothing here repeats it.

Loops: L1 “Past tense? What does he mean?” opens at 0:00 and closes at 0:03 (“They still think we live in teepees”). L2 “So where are Native people today?” opens at 0:00 and closes in the BUTTON (“we're still here. We're here to stay”). Stakes: if violence is not in your own house, it is not on your mind, and October is the month to change that.
do: Open on Cory mid-sentence with the hook text on frame 1.
Keep the pace quick. He talks fast; let him.
Use the two angles: C1 front, C2 side.
Put “Oklahoma City” and “heart of Indian Country” on screen as he says them.
Use only the files named here.
dont: No logo, name or fade at 0:00.
No stock footage of teepees, horses or anything historical. Stay on him and the room.
Do not use the “one in four” number on screen. It is not confirmed by the client.
No Tribal affiliation on the super. Name and title only.
Do not repeat the Durham cut's lines.

client_note: Why this matters: NIWRC's rule is that every visual tells the story and nothing reads as a stereotype. This cut names the stereotype out loud and answers it with the real thing: modern, urban, here.
